name: Layla Colón
life: “I still remember losing a ring while emptying a flooded studio.” On Wednesday, near the brick passage off the shop row, Layla takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I polished the silvering after the shop flooded. A small gray patch hides the dreadful corner where I lost my wedding band.
appearance: Layla is easy to recognize by brown hair pinned away from the temples and a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Usually dressed in a moss-green cardigan with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand, Layla presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Layla has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Layla's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To keep the gray repair visible.
family: Una Curtis is Layla’s stepsibling. Layla gets to change the plan. Una offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *School after sixty*, Una says, “I teach at the university. This is my first attempt to learn bookkeeping and I am the slowest in class.”
connections: Kai Berry. Morning cleaning gives the restorer a chance to explain the gray patch to the widow in private.

reactions.response: Layla asks the tailor and widow what access others would lose if the mirror moved.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Layla offers the worker something dry first and leaves it to them whether to pursue the apology.

reactions.response: Layla seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
reactions.asWritten: If the joke lands badly, Layla seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
